title: Advisory Deprecation without Enforcement (Procrastination Churn)
pattern: Deprecating an API or internal service by applying compiler annotations or warning logs, but allocating no resources, tooling, or enforcement policies to actually migrate callers.
why_bad: Warnings without deadlines or enforcement accumulate indefinitely, leading to "alert fatigue" where developers ignore warnings entirely. Old code remains active and must be maintained forever, dragging down system evolution [721, 723, 728].
detection: Codebases containing long-standing deprecated tags (e.g. `#[deprecated]` older than a major version) with no build-time or commit-time blocks to prevent new invocations.
counterexample: Valid for public open-source libraries with stable ABI guarantees (e.g., standard libraries) where code must be preserved forever [738]. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Move deprecation to a compulsory model with concrete deadlines, backsliding linters (to reject new imports), and actively staffed automated migrations [724, 733, 734].
source: Software Engineering at Google, Chapter 15, "Types of Deprecation - Advisory Deprecation" [721, 723, 728]
